amplitude.name: Amplitude
amplitude.definition: The amplitude of a wave is the greatest distance of a particle from its equilibrium position.
amplitude.example: If you shake a rope harder, its crests rise higher above the equilibrium position, so the amplitude is larger.

contrast.en: Amplitude is half the height from trough to crest, not the full height.
contrast.ru: Амплитуда — половина высоты от впадины до гребня, а не вся высота.

model.en: For sound, use the amplitude of the particles' movement or of the pressure; for light, use the amplitude of the electric or magnetic field.
model.ru: Для звука берут амплитуду колебаний частиц или давления, для света — амплитуду электрического или магнитного поля.

wavelength.name: Wavelength
wavelength.definition: The wavelength is the distance from a point on a wave to the same point on the next wave.

model.en: Measure the distance spanned by several waves, then divide by their number. This way, a small error in one reading matters less.
model.ru: Измерь расстояние, на котором укладывается несколько волн, и раздели его на их число. Так ошибка одного отсчёта меньше влияет на результат.

wavelength.example: From one crest to the next, or one compression to the next.

frequency.name: Frequency
frequency.definition: The number of complete oscillation cycles per second; the unit is hertz (Hz).
frequency.example: The lowest frequency most people can hear is 20 Hz: the source makes 20 complete cycles every second.

model.en: The idea applies to any wave: sound, water waves and light.
model.ru: Понятие относится к любой волне: звуку, волнам на воде и свету.

longitudinal.name: Longitudinal wave
longitudinal.definition: A longitudinal wave is one in which the particles move parallel to the wave's direction of travel.
longitudinal.example: Some earthquake waves, called P-waves, are longitudinal: they push and pull the ground along the direction the wave travels.

model.en: Particles are pushed together where a compression forms and pulled apart where a rarefaction forms. These two regions alternate along the wave.
model.ru: Там, где образуется сгущение, частицы сближаются, а там, где образуется разрежение, расходятся. Эти области чередуются вдоль волны.

transverse.name: Transverse wave
transverse.definition: A transverse wave is one in which the particles move at right angles to the wave's direction of travel.
transverse.example: Other earthquake waves, called S-waves, are transverse: the ground moves from side to side, at right angles to the wave's direction.

model.en: Tension pulls each displaced point back towards its equilibrium position, and that point then pulls its neighbour. The tighter the string, the faster the disturbance moves.
model.ru: Натяжение струны возвращает смещённую точку к положению равновесия, и эта точка, в свою очередь, тянет соседнюю. Чем туже натянута струна, тем быстрее распространяется возмущение.

emSpectrum.name: Electromagnetic spectrum
emSpectrum.definition: The electromagnetic spectrum is the set of all electromagnetic waves, arranged by frequency from radio waves to gamma rays.
emSpectrum.example: Earth's atmosphere lets visible light through, but it absorbs most X-rays and gamma rays from space.

contrast.en: Visible light is only a small part of the spectrum: infrared and ultraviolet waves are electromagnetic too.
contrast.ru: Видимый свет — лишь узкая часть шкалы: инфракрасное и ультрафиолетовое излучение тоже электромагнитные волны.

reflection.name: Reflection
reflection.definition: Reflection is the bouncing back of a wave when it meets a boundary between two media. The reflected wave stays in the original medium.
reflection.example: A ray hits a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 30°. The angle of reflection is also 30°, on the other side of the normal.

model.en: The ray model works when the mirror is much larger than the wavelength.
model.ru: Модель лучей работает, если зеркало намного больше длины волны (wavelength).

contrast.en: Do not confuse it with refraction: the reflected wave keeps its speed, while in refraction the speed changes at the boundary.
contrast.ru: Не путай с преломлением: отражённая волна сохраняет скорость, а при преломлении скорость на границе меняется.

refraction.name: Refraction
refraction.definition: Refraction is the change in direction of a wave at a boundary between two media. It happens when the wave meets the boundary at an angle, because its speed changes.
refraction.example: Light goes from air (n = 1.00) into water (n = 1.33) at 30° to the normal. Its speed drops from 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s to about 2.26 × 10⁸ m/s. The ray bends towards the normal, with an angle of refraction of about 22.1°.

contrast.en: Do not mix up the direction of bending. The ray bends towards the normal when it slows down, and away from it when it speeds up.
contrast.ru: Не путай направление отклонения. Луч приближается к нормали, когда замедляется, и отдаляется от неё, когда ускоряется.

model.en: The refractive index depends on wavelength. Different colours bend by different amounts, so a prism splits white light into colours.
model.ru: Показатель преломления (refractive index) зависит от длины волны. Разные цвета отклоняются на разные углы, поэтому призма разлагает белый свет на цвета.

diffraction.name: Diffraction
diffraction.definition: Diffraction is the spreading of a wave after it passes through a narrow opening or around the edge of an obstacle.
diffraction.example: For sound with a frequency of 1 kHz in air at 20 °C, the wavelength is about 0.34 m. This follows from λ = v / f = 343 m/s ÷ 1000 Hz. Such sound spreads out through a doorway and can be heard in the next room.

contrast.en: Refraction requires a change of wave speed; diffraction can occur in one medium.
contrast.ru: Преломление связано с изменением скорости; дифракция возможна в одной среде.

model.en: Spreading is strong when the opening is about as wide as the wavelength or narrower. Wider openings still show diffraction, but the spreading is smaller.
model.ru: Расхождение сильное, когда ширина отверстия сравнима с длиной волны или меньше её. При более широких отверстиях дифракция всё равно есть, но расхождение меньше.

lens.name: Lens
lens.definition: A lens is a transparent object with curved surfaces that refracts light. A converging lens brings parallel rays together; a diverging lens spreads them apart.
lens.example: A converging lens with f = +10 cm has an object at u = 20 cm. The image is real, at v = 20 cm on the far side, inverted and the same size as the object.

contrast.en: A real image forms where the rays actually cross, so v > 0. A virtual image forms where the backward extensions of the rays meet, so v < 0.
contrast.ru: Действительное изображение возникает там, где лучи реально пересекаются, поэтому v > 0. Мнимое изображение (virtual image) возникает там, где пересекаются продолжения лучей назад, поэтому v < 0.

model.en: Use f > 0 for a converging lens and f < 0 for a diverging lens.
model.ru: Собирающая линза: f > 0; рассеивающая: f < 0.

filter.name: Filter
filter.definition: A filter is a transparent material that absorbs some wavelengths of light and transmits the rest.
filter.example: An ideal red filter under white light transmits red light and absorbs much of the rest.

contrast.en: A filter only absorbs or passes the light that reaches it. It cannot turn one colour into another.
contrast.ru: Светофильтр только поглощает или пропускает свет, который на него падает. Он не превращает один цвет в другой.

model.en: The simulation uses ideal colour bands; real filters have gradual, incomplete transmission and may also reflect light.
model.ru: Модель использует идеальные цветовые диапазоны; у реальных фильтров пропускание неполное и плавно меняется, возможны отражения.

formulas.waveSpeedCaption: Wave speed: v is the speed (m/s), f the frequency (Hz) and λ the wavelength (m).
formulas.periodCaption: Period: T is the time for one complete oscillation (s), f the frequency (Hz).
formulas.snell: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂
formulas.snellCaption: Snell's law: n₁ = refractive index of medium 1, n₂ = refractive index of medium 2 (no units). θ₁ = angle of incidence, θ₂ = angle of refraction; both angles are measured from the normal.
formulas.lensCaption: Thin lens formula: f: focal length; u: object distance; v: image distance; use the same unit for all three, for example cm. Here f is not frequency.

sim1.title: Wave Explorer
sim1.desc: Move the frequency or wavelength slider and watch the product f × λ on the screen: in one medium the wave speed is fixed, so when f goes up, λ goes down.

sim2.title: Reflection & Refraction
sim2.desc: Change the angle, n₁ or n₂: the refracted ray bends towards the normal (dashed line) when n₂ > n₁, and away from the normal when n₂ < n₁. With n₁ > n₂ and an angle above the critical angle, the light undergoes total internal reflection.

sim3.title: Diffraction
sim3.desc: Narrow the slit or lengthen the wavelength to see the waves spread out more. The ratio λ / slit shows how strong the spreading is; the drawing is schematic.

sim4.title: Electromagnetic Spectrum
sim4.desc: Move the slider or press a region name. In a vacuum, c = fλ, so a higher frequency means a shorter wavelength. Region boundaries are approximate.

sim5.title: Converging Lens
sim5.desc: Move the sliders to change the object distance (u) and the focal length (f). A positive image distance (v) means a real image; a negative one means a virtual image. With the object at the focal point, the image is at infinity.

simSound.title: Sound Wave — Pitch & Loudness
simSound.desc: Move the frequency slider to change the pitch, and the amplitude slider to change the loudness. The air particles below show compressions and rarefactions.

simFilters.title: Colour & Filters
simFilters.desc: Choose a light, a filter and an object colour: the observer sees only the colour that passes the filter and is reflected by the object. This is an ideal model: a red filter with blue light gives black.

criteria.title: MYP Criteria
criteria.intro: Four criteria are assessed in MYP Physics. Use the checklists to make sure your response covers everything.

A.title: Criterion A — Knowing & Understanding
A.subtitle: Recall and apply scientific knowledge (the written exam)
items: Recall scientific facts, terms and definitions accurately — vocabulary like 'momentum', 'resultant force', 'refraction' must be used precisely.
Apply scientific knowledge to solve problems in familiar situations (e.g. calculate F = ma when force and mass are given).
Apply scientific knowledge to solve problems in unfamiliar situations (transfer the same idea to a new context, e.g. why an airbag works).
Analyse and evaluate scientific information to make scientifically supported judgements.
Show your working in calculations: formula → substitution → answer → units.
Use the correct command term (state, describe, explain, compare, evaluate, calculate) when answering.

B.title: Criterion B — Inquiring & Designing
B.subtitle: Planning a lab
items: Clear research question with independent, dependent and controlled variables.
Hypothesis with scientific reasoning ('If… then… because…').
Materials and apparatus list with sizes / quantities.
Numbered method that another student could repeat exactly.
Safety considerations identified.
Plan for collecting enough data (≥ 5 values, ≥ 3 repeats).

C.title: Criterion C — Processing & Evaluating
C.subtitle: Analyzing a lab
items: Data table with units in headers and consistent decimal places.
Averages, ranges and uncertainties calculated.
Graph: title, labelled axes, suitable scale, line of best fit.
Trend described in words and linked to the science.
Conclusion answers the research question with evidence.
Evaluation: strengths, weaknesses and realistic improvements.

D.title: Criterion D — Reflecting on the Impacts of Science
D.subtitle: The essay
items: Clear scientific explanation of the issue.
Discussion of social, economic and environmental impacts.
Multiple perspectives considered (for / against / neutral).
Evidence from at least two reliable sources.
Personal opinion with justification.
References listed in a consistent format.
